name: Canadian National Railway

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: CN runs a roughly 20,000-mile freight rail network linking Canada's east and west coasts with the U.S. Midwest and Gulf Coast; it earns money by hauling other people's freight and charging per ton-mile (Q3 2026 freight revenue C$4,574M).

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Seven commodity groups, Q3 2026 share of freight revenue (computed): intermodal 23% (C$1,065M), petroleum and chemicals 22%, grain and fertilizers 20%, metals and minerals 12%, forest products 11%, automotive 6%, coal 5%. FY2025: intermodal largest at 22% of revenue.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: No customer concentration disclosed; MD&A stresses a diversified portfolio with no group above 22% of FY2025 revenue. Buyers are grain exporters, refiners and chemical makers, steel and lumber shippers, automakers and ocean-carrier/retail intermodal customers.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: FY2025 revenue by traffic type: 37% overseas, 29% transborder (Canada-US), 18% Canadian domestic, 16% US domestic. Reports in C$ but a large share of revenue is in US$; a weaker C$ added to Q3 revenue (+15% reported vs +14% constant currency); 17,289 staff in Canada, 6,533 in the US.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Toll-road style network: one reported segment, revenue per ton-mile (7.70 cents in Q3, +10%), fuel surcharges and annual rate increases; heavy fixed network cost. Q3 revenue C$4,771M, operating income C$1,730M.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Operating ratio (costs as % of revenue, lower is better) was 63.7% reported and 61.0% adjusted in Q3 2026 vs 61.4% a year ago; FY2025 61.9%. Capex about C$2.8B net in 2026. Guidance: 2026 adjusted EPS growth 'mid-to-high single digit, tracking toward the upper end'; FY2025 outcome was in line with the July 2025 outlook, so there was a mid-year reset before that.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Fuel: 94.6M US gallons in Q3 at C$6.09 a gallon vs C$3.82 (+59%); fuel cost +56% (C$662M) but CN passed it on through surcharges and rates (revenue per ton-mile +10%) and adjusted OR still improved 40 bp, unlike UNP (-140 bp) and CPKC (-170 bp). Locomotives, rail and rolling stock come from a few suppliers (named in no filing; 40-F risk factor says 'limits the number of suppliers'). Labour: Teamsters Canada Rail Conference (about 6,000 train crews) and Steelworkers (about 2,800 track staff) contracts expire 2026-12-31. Signal tags: oil, diesel, fuel cost, fuel surcharge lag, wages, union contracts, tariffs, steel, capex, dollar.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Only North American railroad touching three coasts (Atlantic, Pacific, Gulf); originates more than 85% and both originates and terminates more than 65% of traffic on its own network. 2026 UP agreement gives CN Kansas City Terminal and St. Louis terminal stakes, Midwest overhead rights, and new Memphis-Eagle Pass (Mexico) access, contingent on the UP-NS merger closing.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Business-to-business freight; shippers pick CN for route and service, not brand. Essential to Canadian exports, but no consumer repeat-buy or pricing premium beyond network position (freight revenue per carload C$3,353, +15%, mostly fuel and mix).

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals: CPKC (Canada-wide, Mexico), UP, BNSF, CSX, NSC. Q3 2026 ton-miles +4% with carloads flat (1,364k vs 1,368k); intermodal ton-miles -3% (CN says it dropped lower-profit international volume; Prince Rupert and Halifax down, Vancouver up). UP-NS merger: CN signed a deal on 2026-07-22 and 'will not oppose' it.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Guide is low single-digit ton-mile growth for 2026 (9-month RTM +4%). Drivers named: grain (record Canadian crop lapping), refined products and NGLs, Mexico access, new crude business; headwinds: flat housing and US tariffs on forest products, weak iron ore. Nothing here suggests growth above mid single digits.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: ROIC 12.9% FY2025; adjusted debt/EBITDA 2.61x (Q3 2026) with Moody's outlook negative; 9-month FCF C$2,918M (+25%) but buybacks C$1,999M plus dividends of about C$1.65B (computed, C$2.745 x ~600M shares) exceed FCF, funded by debt (long-term debt plus current C$22.8B vs C$21.2B at year-end). Buybacks were C$4.55B in 2023, C$2.65B in 2024, C$2.05B in 2025 at roughly US$100-115 a share. Pay: PSUs 70% of long-term pay (40% ROIC, 30% relative TSR); hedging banned; CFO retires 2027-02-01 (planned succession).

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Network cannot be replicated and grain, energy and intermodal flows are structural; main threats are Canadian labour stoppages (a 2024 stoppage hit Q3 2024), blockades, derailments and trade barriers, not loss of relevance. Q3 2026 car velocity 207 (-2%), network speed 19.1 mph (-2%).

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: KPMG audit, disclosure controls and ICFR effective (FY2025 40-F). No 4.01/4.02-type items, NT filings or SEC comment letters in the last 3 years (only a 2021 CORRESP/UPLOAD pair, outside the window). Watch items: Q3 2026 adjustments of C$132M to operating income (impairment, workforce reduction, merger-advisory costs) lift adjusted OR 270 bp below reported; COO change Oct 2025, CFO change Feb 2027.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: positive so far (adjusted EPS +18% in Q3, grain and energy volumes up, surcharges pass fuel through, weaker C$ helps translation). Slowdown: rails hold up better than trucking and fuel costs fall, but Canadian export volumes (grain, forest, intermodal) are cyclical and 2027 labour risk is open. CN assumes C$0.71 and WTI US$80-110 for the rest of 2026. Rates: C$22.8B of mostly fixed-rate debt. Dollar: Q3 constant-currency EPS C$2.14 vs C$2.16 reported.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Teamsters (6,000 crew) and Steelworkers (2,800) contracts expire 2026-12-31; bargaining runs through December and Canadian law lets a strike or lockout follow the statutory process. Also: US tariffs on forest products, CTA cap on grain revenue, Canada-US trade tension. UP-NS docket: CN settled, so it is no longer an opponent (a contrary view in the brief).

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: US$126.40, equity US$75.8B. Reverse DCF on equity (FCF is after interest): TTM FCF about C$3.9B (US$2.78B at 0.71) needs about 11.3% a year for 10 years at 10% discount and 3% terminal growth. CN's own 5-year FCF growth (operating cash flow less property additions, 2020 to 2025: C$3.30B to C$3.34B) is about 0% a year; reported FCF fell from C$3,887M (2023) to C$3,336M (2025). P/E 22.0x trailing and 19.7x forward vs roughly 17-22x own 2022-25 (computed from average price, FX and diluted EPS); EV/EBITDA 10.5x vs CP 12.7x, UNP 15.5x, CSX 15.7x, NSC 15.3x. Cheaper than peers, but price assumes more growth than CN has delivered.

status_reason: Quality is B but price leaves no cushion (needs about 11% FCF growth a year vs about 0% delivered) and there is no identifiable market mistake; revisit after the 2026-12-31 labour contract expiry and Q4 results with 2027 guidance (late January 2027).

feedback.evidence: CN Q3 2026 ton-miles +4%, revenue +15%, grain exports and refined petroleum volumes up, fuel price C$6.09 a gallon vs C$3.82; surcharges and rate increases passed the cost through.

No volume slowdown in CN's data through Q3 and CN reaffirmed 2026 guidance on 2026-10-30; CN itself flags 'heightened demand risk' from trade tensions and tariffs, and forest products are already down (-4% ton-miles).
CN's Q3 fuel cost was +56% y/y and its guidance assumes WTI US$80-110; relief arrives with a lag via lower fuel and later lower surcharges.

No separate regulatory docket read: CN's STB position taken from its own 2026-07-22 release.
